policy: Use the same explicitly configured weak model/provider, temperature and job limits before and after. Start each case from a fresh project; case 8 edits the successful shooter. Keep the Studio preview open. Judge actual playability independently of model prose. Do not use a stronger fallback.

cases.prompt: Create a space shooter: arrow keys move, Space fires, enemies descend, hits score points, contact ends the game, R restarts. Use the built-in ships with correct facing and individual frames.

Create a side-view platformer with running and jumping ranger, solid ground and platforms, a collectible, a lethal hazard, a reachable goal, and R restart. Use actual directional animations and mirror only when permitted.
Create a top-down adventure with four-direction ranger movement, blocking trees, a collectible key, an interactable chest and depth sorting. Keep the last facing direction while idle. R restarts.
Create Breakout with arrow-controlled paddle, Space launch, bouncing ball, destructible blocks, three lives, score, game over and R restart. Use built-in blocks and balls.

Create an offline two-player alternating-turn card matching game using built-in cards. Pointer or arrows select, Space reveals, invalid moves do nothing, matches score, completion shows a result, R restarts.
Create Snake with grid movement, arrow keys, food, score, controlled speed increase, wall/self collision, game over and R restart. Use the neutral template and preserve observable gameplay state.

Create a top-down tank game using the complete built-in tank assembly. Arrow keys move, the tank faces movement, Space fires in that direction, targets take hits and score points, R restarts. Keep one collision proxy and all body parts aligned.
Keep the existing shooter, controls and scoring. Add a slower second enemy wave and a shield power-up without replacing the game from a template. Preserve working sprite selection and restart.
